subject: Agriculture
title: The Combine Harvester
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Combine Harvester usable.

hook.text: A modern combine harvests, threshes, and cleans grain in one pass. It does in hours what once took weeks by hand.

buildup.text: Before combines, harvesting required cutting by scythe, bundling by hand, and threshing with flails—backbreaking labor.

discovery.text: The first successful combine harvester appeared in 1835 in Michigan. By the 1940s, they dominated US grain farming.

twist.text: Modern GPS-guided combines automatically adjust speed and settings based on crop density—harvesting with robotic precision.

climax.text: Custom harvest crews drive combines from Texas to Montana each summer, following the wheat as it ripens northward.

punchline.text: One machine, one operator, 1,000 acres a day. The harvest marathon became a sprint.

quiz.question: What does a combine harvester do?
options: Harvests, threshes, and cleans grain in one pass
